title: Infrastructure Weekly Update - 2026-10-05
content:
Summary:
- Focus this week: stabilize new GPU pool in eu-west-2, finalize Q4 reserved capacity plan, and validate cross-region fallback for Redwood Dedicated customers.
- Net result: eu-west-2 pool live for low-priority Dedicated workloads, single short incident related to NCCL upgrade; capacity forecast updated for Q4 with +18% buffer on critical models.

Highlights / Wins:
- eu-west-2 GPU pool: completed rollout of 48xA100-80GB nodes (mixed q32/qint8 profiles) for Dedicated burst lanes. Initial throughput meets target: median p95 latency within 1.05x of prod eu-west-1 benchmarks for short sequences.
- Autoscaler tuning: new cooldown heuristics reduced oscillations during morning traffic spike (reduced scale-up churn by ~23%).
- Cost ops: preliminary quantization recipe tested on T5-family for reranking workloads - CPU offload reduced per-token GPU time by ~11% in bench runs.

Fleet health and incidents (past 7 days):
- 2026-10-03 03:42 UTC - NCCL library upgrade triggered transient perf regression on 8-node NVLink clusters in us-west-2. Impact: 
  - ~12 minutes increased tail latency for 2 Dedicated customers (no data loss).
  - Root cause: subtle behavior change in peer-to-peer buffer alignment with updated NCCL version.
  - Mitigation: rolled back to previous NCCL build (nccL-2.16.1) on affected clusters; patch PR opened to add validation step to upgrade playbook.
- Hardware: two boards in us-east-1 failed preemptively during burn-in on new servers (vendor swap in progress). Replacement ETA: 2026-10-12. No customer impact due to redundancy.

Regions / Capacity & Planning:
- Current usable GPU count (approx):
  - us-east-1: 720 A100-80GB (production + Dedicated), 120 spare nodes
  - us-west-2: 420 A100-80GB, 40 spare nodes
  - eu-west-1: 300 A100-80GB, 30 spare nodes
  - eu-west-2 (new): 48 A100-80GB (Dedicated burst pool)
- Q4 demand forecast (consolidated): expecting +30% peak token throughput across hosted API and Dedicated baseline vs. Q3. We recommend:
  - Convert 160 spare nodes in us-east-1 to reserved capacity starting 2026-11-01 (finance pre-approval required).
  - Expand eu-west-2 pool to 160 nodes by end of November to improve regional fallbacks and lower cross-region egress for EU customers.
- Routing policy updates: rolling out cost-first fallback rule for non-SLA traffic to prefer qint8 variants in lower-cost regions during sustained >85% utilization windows. Engineering checklist attached to PR #724.

Operational items / Playbooks:
- Upgrade playbook change: add a staged validation run (microbench + long-run KV stress for 30 min) before rolling NCCL or CUDA upgrades across NVLink clusters.
- Incident runbook: include immediate rollback threshold for tail-latency increase >20% for two or more customers.
- Oncall notes: weekend coverage schedule updated - see linked calendar event (infra oncall rotation).

Open work / Blockers:
- eu-west-2 network egress costs: procurement needs clarification on committed bandwidth discounts with the colo provider before we scale beyond 160 nodes. Owner: Maya. Blocker until 2026-10-12.
- Vendor firmware: awaiting vendor sign-off for board replacement batch (us-east-1). Expected delivery 2026-10-12. Hardware team running temporary capacity rebalancing to keep SLAs.
- Quantization validation: applied model quality check (MQC) results show a small regression (0.8% MRR) for one enterprise reranking customer on qint8 recipe - need model team sign-off before enabling auto-quantize in production. Owner: Noah.

Action items (owners):
- Maya: finalize colo bandwidth discount negotiation and share updated cost model by 2026-10-12.
- Noah: complete MQC + eval suite for T5 reranker quantization and submit gating decision by 2026-10-09.
- Olivia: add NCCL upgrade validation job to CI and update upgrade playbook PR by 2026-10-08.
- Liam: prepare reserved capacity proposal for finance (us-east-1 160 nodes) and route for approvals by 2026-10-15.

Next week priorities:
- Finish eu-west-2 capacity scale plan and confirm procurement discounts.
- Roll out improved autoscaler cooldowns to all regions and monitor for two weeks.
- Run a controlled quantization canary with one non-critical Dedicated customer to verify behavioral parity on reranking workload.

Notes / Miscellaneous:
- Bench notes: p50 token time for short-chat sequences (<=128 tokens) in eu-west-2 currently at 6.2ms (p95 19ms) which compares reasonably to eu-west-1 p50 5.8ms (p95 17.6ms).
- Cost note: projected marginal GPU-hour cost for qint8 execution is ~22% lower assuming current reserved pricing and improved batching.
- Reminders: update Confluence 'gpu-fleet-ops' with the NCCL rollback lessons and link the new CI validation job once merged.

Appendix (links):
- Incident timeline (internal notes): confluence://infra/gpu-nccl-2026-10-03
- Capacity spreadsheet: https://sheets.redwood-inference/internal/infra/gpu-capacity-q4
